resources.string: ElevenLabs Scribe turns your speech into text as you talk; Claude can then tidy it up. Your audio and text go to those services under your own API keys, which are stored encrypted on this phone.
Allow the microphone in Voicebar settings
Needs speech-to-text access. Create one at elevenlabs.io under Developers → API keys.
Removes filler words, fixes punctuation and applies spoken corrections (\"Tuesday, no, Wednesday\"). Create a key at console.anthropic.com.
The fastest model works best here.
Paste a new key to replace the saved one
Couldn\'t store the key securely on this phone
Words appear in the text field as you talk, and the polished version replaces them when it\'s ready. Off: words preview in the voice bar and are typed when you finish. Password fields always preview.

Millennial mode: dictated messages never end with a period, because a final period reads as cold. Question marks, exclamation marks and periods between sentences stay. Keep talking after a message and its period comes back before the new words.
Messaging apps (Messages, WhatsApp, Signal, Slack…) and any box whose Enter key sends. Email, notes and everything else keep their periods.
No final period in any field.
While dictating, say “voice bar” and a command as the last thing, then pause. The command runs and isn\'t typed.

While a keyboard is up and you\'re not dictating (Voicebar\'s bar, or Gboard with the way-back button), the phone listens for “voice bar”. The button turns purple; “…listen” (or dictate, start, talk) starts dictating, switching back from Gboard if needed; “…close” (or hide) puts the keyboard away. Runs on the phone, nothing is sent anywhere, and the mic indicator stays on while it listens. Now: %1$s

“Voice bar, done”: finish (polished)
“Voice bar, send”: finish, then send
“Voice bar, keyboard”: finish, then Gboard
“Voice bar, clean up”: polish so far, keep listening
“Voice bar, cancel”: throw it away
“Voice bar, close”: finish, then hide the keyboard
Loose wording works too: “finish”, “send it”, “type”, “polish”, “never mind”, “scratch that”…

Dictation finishes by itself after this long without a recognized word (background noise doesn\'t count). Halfway there (at most 5 seconds in) what you\'ve said so far is cleaned up while it keeps listening; keep talking and the next cleanup sees both, so corrections still work.
Layout, typing with Gboard, the way back
Millennial mode, in chats or everywhere
A text box to practice in
Add an ElevenLabs key to start
A few quick steps: Voicebar for talking, Gboard for typing, and a button on Gboard that brings you back.
Tap Voice and talk. ABC hands you to Gboard for typing; tap Tap to return on Gboard to come back.
Drag to move the cursor · hold still, then drag to select
Selecting · keep a finger down, drag with another to go further
no list price known for that model, so its tokens are counted but not priced

Estimated from what this phone sent, at list prices: Scribe v2 Realtime at $%1$.2f per hour of audio, and %2$s at %3$s. Plan allowances, free hours and credits aren\'t taken into account, so your actual bill can be lower; the ElevenLabs and Claude Console dashboards have the real numbers. Only counts are kept here, never your words or audio.
Create one at elevenlabs.io under Developers → API keys, with speech-to-text access, and paste it here.
Create one at console.anthropic.com under API keys and paste it here.

Tap Voice and talk; the words go straight into the field. Pause and what you\'ve said is polished while it keeps listening. Tap the pill to finish (always polished), swipe it right to finish and send, or swipe it left to throw it away. ⌫ keeps working while you talk. Or say “voice bar, done” (or send, keyboard, clean up, cancel) at the end. It also finishes by itself after a stretch of silence. Slide sideways on the idle Voice pill to move the cursor.

Tap ⌫ to delete a character; tap then hold to keep deleting. With three wide buttons, holding ⌫ opens return, space and delete under your finger; with seven equal buttons, space and return are on the bar and holding ⌫ keeps deleting.
Tap Voice and talk; tap ABC to type with Gboard.
Cursor, keyboard and voice in the middle. Hold delete for space and return.
Space and return on the bar. Hold delete to keep deleting.
Off. Tap to turn on Voicebar in Accessibility settings (if Android says it\'s restricted, allow restricted settings in the app\'s App info first).
Gboard isn\'t turned on as a keyboard. Tap to open keyboard settings.
Turn on Gboard in Android\'s keyboard settings first

While Gboard is open, shows a bar on top of it, a mic in its voice-key spot, or a floating mic bubble; tap it to switch back to Voicebar. It reads only Gboard\'s window: where it is, where its keys are (to find the voice key) and its background color. It doesn\'t read the app you\'re typing in or what you type.
A strip in Gboard\'s own color, joined to its top edge, that says Tap to return
At the end of Gboard\'s top row

A round mic at the right end of Gboard\'s top row, toolbar or suggestions, a little in from the edge; it steps aside for Gboard\'s round buttons there. Gboard\'s own voice key stays where Gboard puts it (turn it off in Gboard ▸ Voice typing if you don\'t want two mics).
A mic bubble above Gboard; drag it anywhere
Turned on. ABC switches to it for typing.

Tap Cursor for a trackpad: drag to move the cursor, hold still then drag to select, and keep one finger down while another drags to go further. Cut, copy, paste and delete sit above it. Tap Done to fold it away.
Settings, switch to another keyboard, and what dictation has cost this month.
Tap ABC and Gboard takes over for typing. Tap to return on Gboard (or the mic in its voice-key spot, or the floating mic) brings Voicebar back, already listening.
Turn on the way back from Gboard
Listen as soon as a text box opens
Dictation starts by itself whenever you tap into a text field, as if you\'d tapped Voice. Not in password fields.
Way back from Gboard is off. Tap to turn it on
